subject: general
question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

My father was always __ordering about my sister.__
solution:
The correct answer is** 'ordering my sister about'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'ordering my sister about'** should be used instead of** 'ordering about my sister'.**
 
• The position of the preposition ‘**about**’ is incorrect in the given sentence it must be placed after the **noun** ‘**sister**’.
 
• The phrase **'ordering about'** means 'to give orders to (someone)'.
 
 
• *Example: You can't just come in here and start **ordering people about.***
 
 
 
• Thus, **‘ordering my sister about’ **is the most appropriate answer.

 

 **Correct Sentence:__** *My father was always** ordering my sister about.***
